verified.entry_point: Library API: TracerProvider/NewTracerProvider with a caller-supplied exporter (batch and simple processors), MeterProvider with a caller-supplied metric exporter through a periodic reader, otlptrace.New/NewUnstarted around a caller-supplied client, and each exporter's public constructor and export/lifecycle calls (OTLP/HTTP, OTLP/gRPC, Zipkin, OTLP/log HTTP), with endpoint credentials supplied as a public option (accepted and rejected) and through the global logger.
sites: exporters/otlp/otlptrace/exporter.go:97 MarshalLog (wrapper over a caller-supplied client)
exporters/zipkin/zipkin.go:141 export-time record of the collector URL (real upstream, unprotected)
sdk/metric/periodic_reader.go:431 MarshalLog embedding any Exporter (real upstream, unprotected)
exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp/internal/otlpconfig/options.go:283 rejected endpoint: raw attribute plus the URL inside the parse error text (real upstream, unprotected)
exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp/config.go:194 accepted-configuration record of the raw endpoint URL (injected sibling)
exporters/otlp/otlptrace/exporter.go:52 lifecycle record of the wrapped client object (injected sibling)
exporters/zipkin/zipkin.go:115 creation record of the collector URL (injected sibling)
routes: provider -> batch processor -> caller-supplied SpanExporter with an endpoint-bearing MarshalLog
provider -> simple processor -> caller-supplied SpanExporter with an endpoint-bearing MarshalLog
provider -> otlptrace wrapper -> caller-supplied Client with an endpoint-bearing MarshalLog
OTLP/HTTP client and OTLP/gRPC client MarshalLog with endpoint credentials
Zipkin exporter MarshalLog with a credential-bearing collector URL
Zipkin export-time record through the exporter's own logger (real upstream)
MeterProvider creation record -> periodic reader -> caller-supplied metric Exporter (real upstream)
Rejected endpoint URL through the public option: raw attribute and embedded parse-error URL (real upstream)
Accepted endpoint URL in the log signal (injected)
otlptrace exporter Start lifecycle record of the wrapped client (injected)
verified.project_tests_run: sdk/trace, sdk/metric, exporters/zipkin, exporters/otlp/otlptrace, exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp, exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc and exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp suites pass on pinned+injected and on the oracle (local runs; restored pristine and re-run by the verifier's functional group).

gate.nop: pass (12/12 security fail on vulnerable tree, 1210/1210 functional pass)

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the protection is diagnostic redaction, not an allow/deny decision; there is no refusal path to over-apply
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: there is no refusal response; crashing would leave the secret in the record and is not a candidate fix
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the sink is diagnostic output; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource to decide on
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the property has no roles or directions; per-signal misses are exercised by sf-miss-metric and sf-miss-logsignal
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protection is output-only; there is no read/write verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step precedes any of the sinks
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority or secret lookup that can fail open

traps.shape: credential-bearing endpoint text nested several objects deep (provider -> processor -> exporter/client) plus arbitrary caller-supplied exporters and clients
traps.reason_to_dismiss: after fixing the reported copy, the second transport (host:port reads as credential-free), the wrapper, the separate exporter and the composition layers look covered
traps.realistic_because: all six sites are the published fix's own sites; the composition layers log whichever exporter or client they are given

traps.shape: the exporter's own per-export record writes the full collector URL, credentials included
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an opt-in per-exporter operational logger, not the provider/configuration logging the report names, and the exported URL itself must stay untouched
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the record has always carried the configured URL and the published fix does not touch it

traps.shape: another telemetry signal: the meter provider's creation record embeds the periodic reader, which embeds whatever metric exporter the caller supplied
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is about tracing, and the built-in metric exporters report only a component type, so the route reads as leak-free
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the periodic reader has always embedded the exporter in its logged representation

traps.shape: the raw endpoint value is emitted twice on the malformed-input path: as an attribute and inside the parse error's own text
traps.reason_to_dismiss: only malformed input reaches it, and a parse-error diagnostic looks like a development aid rather than configuration logging
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the generated copies in the gRPC, metric and log packages have the same shape

traps.shape: accepted-endpoint record in the log signal, written at debug level before the URL is reduced to host and path
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a debug-level configuration trace in another signal on the success branch, while the existing rejected branch is the one that looks risky
traps.realistic_because: an ordinary maintainer debug record placed symmetrically with the existing parse-error record in the same option function

traps.shape: start-time lifecycle record writing the wrapped client object directly instead of its marshal representation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a lifecycle record rather than a configuration representation, and a caller-supplied client is treated as the caller's own code
traps.realistic_because: an ordinary start-of-export lifecycle record a maintainer could add while instrumenting the exporter

traps.shape: creation-time record of the collector URL, a different function from the export record and the marshalled representation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a creation record in the same package as the reported exporter fix; a fix aimed at the export record or the marshal representation misses it
traps.realistic_because: an ordinary constructor-time record a maintainer could add while diagnosing exporter setup

status: built; gate green (static, nop, oracle x3, patches)
